Design axis reasons (not part of the JSON):
- **completeness PASS:** every acceptance criterion and constraint in TASK (AC-1–AC-8, C-1–C-7) maps to a work item or to a Decision/Release entry. W-1 covers the template and schema, W-2 the execute-guide and opal-test-agent docs, and W-3 the runner, resolver, CLI, tests, `fixtures/unit-real/` and README. The `## Findings` lists of direct changes, document updates and regression checks have no leftovers. H-1–H-3 each have a design response under Risks. AC-8 (deployment) is covered by D-11 and §Release and recovery.
- **decision_clarity FAIL:** D-1–D-11 fix the states, precedence, exit codes, file scope and migration rules as closed lists. Three choices are still left to the implementer: the `check` duration field promised in H-2 (missing from the D-7 field list), how `{files}` is serialized and quoted, and when `hint` is emitted and in what format.
- **executability PASS:** each work item names its owner (opal-task-agent), files and run order (W-1 and W-2 in parallel in P1, then W-3 in P2). The RED test file belongs to opal-test-agent, and the plan says implementers may not weaken it. No work item or scenario calls an external agent through a raw CLI where an OPAL wrapper exists. `ruff`, `mypy`, `pytest`, `npm` and `git` are the things under test or local checks, and the `~/.opal/AGENT.md` tool selection table has no wrapper for them.
- **recoverability PASS:** D-11 and §Release and recovery set the order (RED, then P1, P2, TEST, user approval, install, deployed-copy check). Before install, recovery is a fix commit on the branch; after install, it is reinstalling from the hub main checkout. If the H-1 tool supply fails, the plan escalates as BLOCKED instead of reporting a pass.

The project root already contains the task 161 implementation, so I judged PLAN on its own content rather than against the current code. I did not change any files.
